item.title: You'll Laugh, You'll Cry, Stop.
item.content:encoded:
I have to say… this is actually one of my favorite SCPs. I tend to like the articles that are aimed at more complex emotions than fear or shock or confusion, and this story of friendship and anomalous sapience does exactly that. If there ever were to be an SCP TV show, I would gladly see an episode devoted to this. It's a beautiful exploration in what the form is capable of.

+1, and keep up the good work.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Edits are announced in discussion threads, a crosslink tag exists that shows all articles currently in the seven day feedback phase, authors are given a PM at the start of the feedback phase, and at the end, links have been posted to our list of upcoming proposals, and links have been posted for our link of finished crosslinks, so there is no shortage of ways for the community at large to learn about and discuss these proposals.

As someone who has been doing a lot of these proposals, no one commenting on a crosslink proposal is not uncommon, at all, and certainly is not an outlier. While Scorpion is correct that some of them do get pretty heated, many get zero comments, or just an "Okay" from the author. Definitely not something I would be concerned with. Additionally, authors always have a right to change any edits made as part of the WikiWalk project at any time.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Definitely an outlier from what I've seen. Discussions on some of these can get quite… um…passionate.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

Both this article, and SCP-2246 involve SCPF personnel (or D-Class as the case may be) befriending a anomaly as it produces writing. Such an occurrence may happen again, and I like to think that the Foundation keeps protocols for what to do in such recurring situations, so its not that far out there to see these articles being linked by this protocol. As such, I am proposing the following edit:

Changing the following:

SCP-696 regularly requests to communicate with D-69601 and have him load it with paper and red ink for non-communicative purposes, citing a desire to write a novel for others to read. Permission was temporarily granted to test whether non-communicative products of SCP-696 possessed anomalous properties.

To this:

SCP-696 regularly requests to communicate with D-69601 and have him load it with paper and red ink for non-communicative purposes, citing a desire to write a novel for others to read. Permission was temporarily granted to test whether non-communicative products of SCP-696 possessed anomalous properties. D-69601 has been briefed on appropriate Snow Protocols, which are to remain active throughout the duration of testing.

The name Snow comes from Phoenix Snow, the anomalous writer at the heart of SCP-2246.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't recall reading the original, so I can't say how this version compares. However, even on its own merits, it one doesn't do anything for me. The "harmless thing that threatens you" bit has already been done much better with Pesterbot, and the interview, which I assume was meant to be funny, didn't even make me crack a smile. The only thing that I can count in its favor are that it didn't involve a great deal of meta-textual wankery about writing for the site and what it means. I was afraid that you were going down that path when I read the first interview, but was relieved to find that you avoided it. Unfortunately, "Not doing a thing" is insufficient reason for me to upvote or to cancel my downvote, so -1 it is.

item.title: FINALLY INDEED
item.content:encoded:
So after reading "YOUR TIME IS NIGH. IF YOU HAVE A GOD, PRAY TO IT NOW." I knew I had to rewrite this thing, and keep that line. I mean, how do you not keep that line? It's perfect. People liked the ham on the old version, and by jove I've given you ham. Almost literally- the original version of the rewrite had the typewriter be made of pork products.

Thanks to Riemann, Weizhong, Randomini, and probably a bunch of other people for reading the draft. Special thanks to ksaid for helping with the horrible, horrible prose.

I can't entirely remember the context of this. A typo making some random word "car," I think.
